scope: Every ratio compares the medians of three samples per role from one matched runner; paired trial values and runner identities remain separate. No durations, distributions, ratios or speedups are pooled across jobs or source snapshots.

These experiments directly compare the immutable original 96e baseline against the explicit legacy-composite path in the immutable 0ffa candidate. They do not measure or change the candidate's default persistent path.

The completed selection comparison regresses in elapsed duration despite lower renderer-thread CPU. Passing source, input and native-pixel correctness contracts does not qualify baseline recovery or default promotion.

Six primary samples determine each comparison. The candidate's one managed-diagnostic pass is separate and excluded from all primary medians and ratios. Hover and selection require zero Document paints and actual cache reuse; camera/edit workloads require actual Document paints.

Every measured trial retains the full original common pan warmup and native before/after/restored validation. These 45 pairs cover the Welcome timing fixture at DPR 1; broader lifecycle, fractional-DPR and extended-SVG gates are separate.
All primary windows exclude startup, common warmup, capture, restore and drain operations. Total experiment duration includes those phases and diagnostics, so it is not a sum of primary windows.
ThreadTime measures active renderer main-thread CPU and excludes GPU and worker CPU. TaskDuration is elapsed task time and can include waits. Neither is native GPU execution time.

Offered operations per second, completed callbacks and visible-canvas submissions are not physical presentation or proven input-to-new-pixels latency. The existing no-tail gates only establish later callback and graphics observations after every trusted input.

Upload call counts and supplied JavaScript buffer bytes are API observations rather than measured physical transfer bytes. All raw observer data, complete console logs and native PNGs remain bound to the immutable source reports and artifact digests.
